stories.event: COP31, the UN climate conference in Antalya (Türkiye presidency, Australia leading negotiations), was scheduled to close on Friday 20 November 2026. On Thursday the presidency published a 9-page second draft of the cover decision ('Antalya Declaration') that drops all fossil-fuel wording and the $120bn adaptation-finance target but keeps a goal of 35% electricity share of final energy by 2035; Reuters says it is not the final version. Panama has threatened in writing to block any deal without a cap on global oil production, while the EU reconvenes ministers on Friday; the last two COPs ended on Saturday and Sunday.

research.question: Is the COP31 closing plenary expected Friday night or Saturday? Has a new text appeared, how has the EU reacted to the 19 Nov draft, and does Panama threaten to block it? (One entry used for both cop31-adopt-22 and cop31-fossil-22.)
research.finding: Nothing new beyond the dossiers as of ~18:15Z Thu 19 Nov. No third draft and no closing-plenary time announced; no outlet read gives a schedule. RTE (modified 17:27Z 19 Nov): EU ministers chaired by Ireland's Darragh O'Brien met after the second draft and 'would continue examining the document throughout the evening, with ministers reconvening tomorrow' (Fri 20 Nov). Hoekstra said the EU will judge the draft against three tests (1.5C response, implementation, the EU mandate) and declined to say whether the EU will insist that fossil-fuel wording go back in. So the EU has not demanded it yet, and its position comes Friday. AFP/France24 (13:30Z 19 Nov): talks 'formally close Friday' but often run over; Panama threatened on Thursday to block any deal that does not meet its demands, including a cap on global oil production. Reuters/Globe and Mail (14:13Z): the second draft is 'not expected to be the final version'; recent COPs 'regularly blown past this deadline by more than 24 hours'. UN News (19 Nov): 'On the eve of the summit's scheduled close, ministers and the Presidency were still trying to bridge sharp differences.' Common Dreams (17:35Z): the words 'fossil fuels' appear nowhere in the 19 Nov draft, which offers only a 'transition towards low greenhouse gas emissions and climate-resilient development'. NGOs (Greenpeace, Oil Change, 350.org, Power Shift Africa 'ghost COP') call it unacceptable. No report of AOSIS/LDC demands since then. ENB (403), the Guardian (403) and BusinessGreen (403) could not be read; the Climate Home bulletin is paywalled.

research.question: Is the COP31 closing plenary expected Friday night or Saturday? Has a new text appeared, how has the EU reacted to the 19 Nov draft, and does Panama threaten to block it? (One entry used for both cop31-adopt-22 and cop31-fossil-22.)
research.finding: Nothing new beyond the dossiers as of ~18:15Z Thu 19 Nov. No third draft and no closing-plenary time announced; no outlet read gives a schedule. RTE (modified 17:27Z 19 Nov): EU ministers chaired by Ireland's Darragh O'Brien met after the second draft and 'would continue examining the document throughout the evening, with ministers reconvening tomorrow' (Fri 20 Nov). Hoekstra said the EU will judge the draft against three tests (1.5C response, implementation, the EU mandate) and declined to say whether the EU will insist that fossil-fuel wording go back in. So the EU has not demanded it yet, and its position comes Friday. AFP/France24 (13:30Z 19 Nov): talks 'formally close Friday' but often run over; Panama threatened on Thursday to block any deal that does not meet its demands, including a cap on global oil production. Reuters/Globe and Mail (14:13Z): the second draft is 'not expected to be the final version'; recent COPs 'regularly blown past this deadline by more than 24 hours'. UN News (19 Nov): 'On the eve of the summit's scheduled close, ministers and the Presidency were still trying to bridge sharp differences.' Common Dreams (17:35Z): the words 'fossil fuels' appear nowhere in the 19 Nov draft, which offers only a 'transition towards low greenhouse gas emissions and climate-resilient development'. NGOs (Greenpeace, Oil Change, 350.org, Power Shift Africa 'ghost COP') call it unacceptable. No report of AOSIS/LDC demands since then. ENB (403), the Guardian (403) and BusinessGreen (403) could not be read; the Climate Home bulletin is paywalled.

research.question: Which UKMTO incidents occurred on 18-19 Nov, and is the tempo changing?
research.finding: 18 Nov was not quiet. UKMTO logged a second incident: a time-delayed report published late on 18 Nov (Arab News 23:12Z; TASS) of a tanker 'struck by an unknown projectile in the engine room while transiting outbound' about 6 nm north of Khasab, crew safe. Escalation signals on 19 Nov: Iranian strikes on Bahrain and Kuwait (The National, PBS); a Houthi strike on a Riyadh financial-district tower and Saudi strikes on Sanaa; the IRGC says it will not allow the US blockade to continue; the US widened the blockade to ship-to-ship transfers; a houseofsaud.com headline says Muscat talks failed.
